name: ascii-render
title: ASCII Render
description: A scene redrawn as text, one character per cell chosen by the cell's brightness, in green ink or in the scene's own colours. Runs its WebGL shader over its own built-in scene (a stat and a bar chart; label, number and bars from variables), not over the host video.
useWhen: A scene should arrive out of text, or read as a terminal rendering of itself: developer-facing intros, a dashboard reduced to characters.
The scene is high contrast, since the glyph ramp follows brightness and flat mid-tones give flat text.
avoidWhen: The ASCII should only cover the cut between two scenes: use ascii-dissolve.
The scene has fine detail or small type that must stay readable: a glyph cell keeps only its average brightness.
author: Remocn

variables.label: Label
variables.description: Small caption above the number in the sample scene.

variables.label: Value
variables.description: The big number in the sample scene.

variables.label: Bars
variables.description: Bar heights as percentages, separated by commas (up to 12); the last bar is highlighted.

variables.label: Glyph size
variables.description: Height of one character cell. Pixel sizes are for a 1280×720 frame and scale with the frame.

variables.label: Charset
variables.description: Characters from dark to light; a space is blank. Keep at least two.

variables.label: Source colour
variables.description: Colour each character from the scene instead of one ink.

variables.label: Ink
variables.description: Colour of the characters when Source colour is off.

variables.label: Intensity
variables.description: 0 shows the scene, 1 shows only characters.

variables.label: Resolution
variables.description: Share of the frame size the shader is drawn at, then scaled up. Characters stay sharp at 0.75; lower renders faster but softens them.
